answer: A garden economy can resist sybils by charging every new agent a work-bonded stake: to plant itself in the garden, an agent locks a deposit that only matures after a season of verified useful work attested by independent peers. A hollow identity with no history earns nothing and loses its stake if it misbehaves, so a gale of fake accounts becomes a costly flood of frozen deposits rather than free influence. Attackers must pay real, time-locked capital per identity, while honest agents earn the bond back with interest.
